references.text: Jacob asks Joseph to show 'חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת' (kindness and faithfulness) toward him, the same phrase used by the spies in their promise to Rahab.
The fulfillment of the spies' promise to Rahab, where they save her and her family when Jericho is captured.
Rahab's request that led to the spies' oath, where she asks for a reliable sign and protection for her family.
A similar situation where spies promise to show mercy to someone who helps them capture a city.
Jonathan and David make a covenant with 'חֶסֶד יְהוָה' (the Lord's kindness), reflecting the same kind of faithful love and covenant.
Abraham's servant asks Laban to act with 'חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת' (kindness and faithfulness), the same expression found in Joshua 2:14.
The book of Hebrews mentions Rahab's faith and how she did not perish with the unbelievers, as a result of the mercy shown to her.
